I've written the report to `/mnt/black/prog/agent-skills/.worktrees/refresh-catalog-haiku-5-5/docs/casebook/2026-10-08__fe46a1e7/research-claude-opus-5-5.md`. Nothing was committed, as the brief asked.

**Verdict:** Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5. At the same price as GPT-6 Luna it is smarter, and it is the fastest model in the roster. It is the right pick for short, well-scoped subagent work at low or medium effort.

**It's not a cheap stand-in for coding loops.** On Cognition's coding benchmark, GPT-6.1 Sol at medium effort scores higher than Haiku at max effort for about a quarter of the cost, because Haiku uses so many tokens. Prompts over 100K tokens also cost 5x, which long agent sessions will probably hit (that part is my inference).

**Limits:**
- Independent data is thin, since the model is a day old.
- The coding-benchmark figures come from one launch partner, and I got them secondhand.
- One page wouldn't load, so the Vals AI numbers are secondhand too.
- I couldn't read the existing `models.md`, so I placed the model from web sources only.

**No other new model shipped since Oct 4.** OpenAI did post new versions of GPT-6 Sol and Luna, but only with safety data. Claude Code 2.1.293 also made Haiku 5.5 its default Haiku, which matters for `tools.md`.
